archetypes.name: cross-doc-trailer-contract
archetypes.rationale: The new optional trailer grammar must be stated identically across check-plan-size.md, SKILL.md, flags.md, approval-gates.md, and discussion-rounds.md — subtle divergences between these five surfaces are the primary plan-defect risk for this change.
archetypes.prompt_body: Verify that the exact trailer grammar (anchored regexes ^diff_added: [0-9]+$, ^diff_deleted: [0-9]+$, ^mechanical_churn: (true|false)$), the contiguous-block scanning rule (stop at first non-matching line including blanks), the last-match-wins tie-breaker, and the PLAN_LINES subtraction contract are stated with identical semantics in every file the plan touches: check-plan-size.md, SKILL.md, flags.md, approval-gates.md, and discussion-rounds.md. Look for subtle divergences — e.g., one file says 'blank lines stop scanning' while another implies they are skipped, or one threshold is stated as >= while another uses strict >. Check whether any cross-doc reference chain (e.g., approval-gates.md pointing to check-plan-size.md) would leave a consumer with incomplete or contradictory information if they read only one file. Flag cases where the plan says to 'update' a file but does not spell out the new canonical wording precisely enough to prevent drift between the five surfaces. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: acceptance-test-gap
archetypes.rationale: The plan's ~12 acceptance criterion bullets must each map to a specific automated test case; gaps mean criteria that can only be verified manually, and the plan's own failure-mode analysis names several 'earliest signal' assertions that may have no corresponding test.
archetypes.prompt_body: Cross-map each bullet in the Acceptance section of the plan to the specific test cases described for test-check-plan-size.sh and test-design-structure.sh. Identify acceptance criteria that have no corresponding automated test case — e.g., the claim that emit-plan.sh, design-driver.sh, diff-lines.txt, and composed-plan.md contracts are unchanged, or that the hard prompt stays two-option with no Continue. Also check whether the plan's Failure Modes section identifies failure signals ('Earliest signal: ...') that are not covered by any named test case or spot-check, since an undetected failure mode is a plan defect even if the implementation is correct. Flag cases where a test case is described only as a 'spot-check' when the plan's own failure-mode analysis characterizes it as a regression risk requiring automated coverage. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: revision-path-coverage
archetypes.rationale: Three distinct plan-revision paths (Gate A discussion, Gate B apply-all, revise-plan-with-waterfall.sh) must each preserve optional trailers — missing any one silently converts a mechanical/deletion-heavy plan back to legacy hard-trigger behavior after any revision.
archetypes.prompt_body: Verify that every code path that can rewrite plan.txt and re-invoke check-plan-size.sh is explicitly covered by the plan's preservation contract: Gate A discussion rounds (discussion-rounds.md), Gate B apply-all (approval-gates.md), the waterfall file-replacement logic in revise-plan-with-waterfall.sh, and any other plan-revision entry points visible in the file list. Check whether the mitigation for Failure Mode 4 (revision-flow trailer loss) is enforced mechanically — i.e., whether the plan adds validation code or only prompt prose, and whether prompt prose alone is sufficient to prevent a revision agent from dropping the trailers. Confirm the automated regression in test-revise-plan-with-waterfall.sh covers both rejection of a candidate that drops optional trailers and acceptance of a candidate that preserves them, rather than leaving this as a manual spot-check. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
